channel.title: The Forge
channel.description: A daily hour. Private curriculum, built for one listener.
channel.itunes:author: Prinz

item.title: [Practical Geography] How to Read a Map Beyond the Blue Dot
item.description: Original fictional park and paper exercises develop scale arithmetic, distance versus route length, local coordinates, contour geometry, ascent, gradients, bearings and route networks. Five recall pauses with answers and a desk-based map exercise. Selected source material consulted: Ordnance Survey Map Reading, sections on scale, grids, contours and compass references, https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/documents/resources/map-reading.pdf ; USGS Topographic Mapping, topographic-map and scale discussion, https://www.usgs.gov/educational-resources/topographic-mapping ; Ordnance Survey explanation of true, grid and magnetic north, https://www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/news/three-norths-align-great-britain. Historical production details and old magnetic correction values are not presented as current. All park locations, route lengths, access conditions, travel rates and event timings are invented teaching examples, not actual navigation or accessibility advice. No full-book coverage claimed.

item.title: [Communication] How to Give Feedback That Improves the Work
item.description: Original fictional studio, presentation, invitation and handover cases teach specific observations, shared standards, diagnosis, priorities, feasible deadlines, review authority, disagreement, version control and followup. Includes five recall pauses with answers and a short revision exercise. Selected source passages consulted: Hattie and Timperley, The Power of Feedback (2007), opening definition and discussion of task/process information, https://assess.ucr.edu/sites/g/files/rcwecm2336/files/2019-02/hattietimperley_2007.pdf ; Shute, Focus on Formative Feedback, ETS Research Report RR-07-11 (March 2007), abstract and sections 3.3 to 3.5 on specificity, verification, elaboration and complexity, https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ1111586.pdf. These educational reviews provide limited background, not experimental validation of the original workplace examples. No full-book coverage claimed. Informal audience counts are illustrative and do not establish causal improvements in bookings.

item.title: [Business & Systems] Why Queues Grow Before You Run Out of Capacity
item.description: Run a fictional repair workshop through arrival bursts, variable repair durations, backlog recovery, Little's law, a clearly specified M/M/1 model, serial bottlenecks, shared labour, batching, pooled queues, priority rules and rework. Original event schedules and exact numerical comparisons distinguish waiting, service, turnaround and useful output. Five recall pauses with answers and a paper scheduling exercise. Sources actually consulted: Larson and Odoni, Urban Operations Research, section 4.3, https://web.mit.edu/urban_or_book/www/book/chapter4/4.3.html ; MIT 6.02 Lecture 17 (2009), section 17.4.1 on Little's law, https://web.mit.edu/6.02/www/s2009/handouts/L17.pdf ; MIT 1.041 queueing-model slides (2026), selected definitions, stationarity, Little's law, M/M/1 assumptions and derivation, https://web.mit.edu/1.041/www/lectures/L8-queuing-models-2026sp.pdf. No source case studies or passages are reproduced. Bench Street and all worked cases are original hypothetical illustrations; precise queue-model predictions apply only under their stated assumptions.

item.title: [Spiritual Traditions] The Bhagavad Gita on Action, Duty and Attachment
item.description: Begin with Arjuna's moral conflict and follow the Gita's account of duty, the enduring self, action without attachment, meditation, devotion and the three qualities of nature. Original community-performance examples distinguish responsible action from dependence on praise or indifference to consequences. Five recall questions with pauses and answers, plus a small reflective application. Source consulted: Bhagavad Gita, Edwin Arnold's public-domain poetic translation The Song Celestial, selected chapters I, II, III, V, VI, IX, XII, XIV and XVIII, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/2388/pg2388-images.html . Edition and translator information: https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2388. This is a focused reading through one historical English translation, not coverage of the whole work or every Hindu interpretation. Metaphysical and devotional teachings are presented as teachings; modern cases and arithmetic are original illustrations.

item.title: [Chemistry] What Actually Burns in a Candle
item.description: Follow wax from the solid reservoir through capillary flow, gaseous fuel and combustion. Explain where the candle mass goes, why reaction products outweigh the fuel, how bonds and activation barriers relate to energy, and how mixing creates the visible flame. Original methane, model-wax and propane inventories; worked power calculations; five recall pauses with answers and a paper-only application. Sources consulted: selected lectures in Michael Faraday, The Chemical History of a Candle, edited by William Crookes (public domain), https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/14474/pg14474-images.html ; OpenStax Chemistry 2e, Paul Flowers, Klaus Theopold, Richard Langley and William R. Robinson, selected sections 4.1, 5.1, 7.5 and 12.5 (consulted for factual verification), https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/4-1-writing-and-balancing-chemical-equations ; https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/5-1-energy-basics ; https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/7-5-strengths-of-ionic-and-covalent-bonds ; https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/12-5-collision-theory ; American Chemical Society, Shining a Light on Candles, https://inchemistry.acs.org/atomic-news/shining-light-on-candles.html. Explanations and numerical cases are original. No prior reading or home combustion experiment required.

item.title: [Applied Practice] Write a Scene That Changes the Story
item.description: Develop the original theatre story The Wrong Name from a vague argument into a complete confrontation and earned ending. Apply the published September 21 storytelling lesson through objectives, viewpoint, subtext, changing tactics, scene timing, alternative endings and sentence revision. Eighty substantive teaching turns, five recall pauses with answers, and a short fictional writing exercise. Sources actually consulted: selected plot sections of Aristotle’s Poetics, translated by S. H. Butcher, https://www.gutenberg.org/files/1974/1974-h/1974-h.htm ; selected viewpoint and dialogue passages in Edith Wharton’s The Writing of Fiction, https://www.gutenberg.org/files/72446/72446-h/72446-h.htm . Original examples and modern exercises are adaptations, not quotations or universal rules. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Geography] Why Rivers Flood After the Rain Stops
item.description: Follow water through the fictional town of Bellford. Learn catchments, rainfall volume, infiltration, groundwater, discharge, river stage, hydrographs, tributary timing, finite storage and annual flood probability. Original calculations and contrasting cases explain why the same rain can produce different floods. Includes five recall pauses with answers and a paper catchment exercise. No prior reading required. Sources actually consulted: selected USGS Water Science School explanations at https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school ; Environment Agency natural flood management summaries at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/natural-flood-management-evidence/river-and-floodplain-management ; and US National Weather Service flood safety guidance at https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood-turn-around-dont-drown . This is an introductory geography lesson, not a local flood forecast or engineering design.

item.title: [Technology] What Happens When You Open a Website
item.description: Follow a fictional poster shop from a browser request to the visible page. Learn how Wi-Fi, DNS, packets, routing, TCP, TLS, HTTP, browser rendering, caching, cookies and QUIC cooperate, and why a page can partly work. Includes original transfer calculations, five recall questions with answers and a paper troubleshooting exercise. No prior reading required. Source material consulted: selected sections of the IETF RFC specifications for DNS, IP, TCP, TLS, HTTP and QUIC at https://www.rfc-editor.org/ ; selected MDN web mechanics, HTTP and performance documentation at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web ; and Google web.dev guidance on layout shifts at https://web.dev/articles/optimize-cls . This is an original introductory lesson, not a complete networking course or a reading of those documents.

item.title: [Biology] How Cell Membranes Control What Gets In
item.description: Build an imaginary cell on paper to understand lipid bilayers, diffusion, channels and carriers, electrical gradients, osmosis, ATP-powered pumps, coupled transport and vesicles. Five recall questions with answers and a paper application. Original dialogue, examples and arithmetic; no prior reading required. References consulted: selected sections of Biology 2e by Mary Ann Clark, Matthew Douglas and Jung Choi, OpenStax, and section 12.7 of College Physics for AP Courses. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/1-introduction . Also selected passages of General Principles of Secondary Active Transporter Function by Oliver Beckstein and Fiona Naughton: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.06275 .

item.title: [Business] When More Sales Mean Less Profit
item.description: Follow an original bag-workshop case through contribution, break-even, discounts, price changes, special orders, scarce capacity and product mix. Includes five recall questions with answers and a fictional portrait-editing pricing exercise. No prior reading required. Reference: selected sections 3.1-3.5, 10.1, 10.2 and 10.6 of Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting, by Mitchell Franklin, Patty Graybeal and Dixon Cooper, OpenStax. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/principles-managerial-accounting/pages/1-why-it-matters . Original dialogue, scenarios and calculations, not copied textbook problems.

item.title: [Electricity] Why a Battery Can Light a Bulb
item.description: Understand charge, current, voltage, resistance and power through original paper circuits. Calculate series and parallel networks, voltage-divider loading, internal resistance and energy use. Five recall questions with answers and a worked paper exercise. Scientific reference: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, College Physics 2e, OpenStax, sections 20.1-20.4, 21.1, 21.2 and 21.4. Access free at https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/1-introduction-to-science-and-the-realm-of-physics-physical-quantities-and-units . Original examples and dialogue; no copied textbook exercises.

item.title: [Philosophy] How Epictetus Handles Setbacks and Other People
item.description: Explore Epictetus’s Enchiridion through a musician facing travel disruption, criticism, ambition and conflicting commitments. Explains agency, judgement, responsibility, impermanence and practice with five recall questions and a paper exercise.

item.title: [Applied Practice] Fill the Workshop Without Overpromising
item.description: Build a clear invitation and a dependable enquiry-to-booking workflow for a fictional beginner workshop. Applies the published AI and persuasion lessons through event records, genuine social proof, current availability, retrieval, confirmed actions and worked cases. Five recall questions with answers and a paper exercise.

item.title: [Economics] How Specialisation and Trade Create Value
item.description: Smith and Ricardo explained through original festival and booklet cases. Learn division of labour, market size, opportunity cost, comparative advantage, trade terms, bottlenecks and adjustment costs. Five recall questions with worked answers and a private paper exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Spiritual Traditions] The Kybalion’s Seven Principles Explained
item.description: The All, mental creation and the seven principles explained through close reading and an original pottery workshop case. Distinguishes the book's metaphysical claims from modest practical adaptations. Five recall questions with answers and a private paper exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Relationships] How to Flirt and Build a Mutual Connection
item.description: Conversation, flirting and dating through original adult exhibition and cafe cases. Learn how to express interest, make clear invitations, adapt to different responses, explore compatibility and recognise pressure. Brief research discussions on liking and responsiveness, plus a clearly labelled comparison with Deida's polarity framework. Five recall questions with answers and a paper dialogue exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Physics] Why the Same Music Sounds Different Around a Room
item.description: Sound explained through speakers, reflections, room modes and musical instruments. Work through frequency, wavelength, pressure, phase, resonance, harmonics and beats using original numerical examples. Five recall questions with answers and a paper room-model exercise. Selected classical acoustics passages checked against modern physics references; no prior physics knowledge required.

item.title: [History] How Augustus Ruled Rome Without Calling Himself King
item.description: How Augustus combined provincial military command, public powers, money and prestige while republican offices survived. Explains the settlements of 27 and 23 BCE, veterans, public works and succession. Includes five recall questions with answers and a historical power-map exercise. Based on selected passages from Polybius, Augustus and Cassius Dio, with museum context. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Creativity] How Stories Build Tension and Meaning
item.description: Build an original music-box story through consequential choices, viewpoint, dialogue, scene and summary, and an earned ending. Includes contrasting drafts, five recall questions with answers, and a short scene-writing exercise. Craft references: selected sections of Aristotle's Poetics and Edith Wharton's The Writing of Fiction. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Applied Practice] Make the Job Work: Time, Cash and Clear Agreements
item.description: Sunday application of the published September 14 habits, September 15 cash-flow and September 16 negotiation lessons. Work through an original print-studio project from enquiry to payment, then contrast a family keepsake project. Five recall questions with answers and a fictional one-page planning exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Persuasion] Why Favours, Crowds and Scarcity Change Decisions
item.description: Reciprocity, social proof and scarcity explained through research and original workshop examples. Covers useful samples, relevant testimonials, real availability, decision-making and measured outcomes. Five recall questions with answers and a fictional invitation exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [AI & Technology] How Language Models Turn Words into Answers
item.description: Inside a language model: tokens, embeddings, attention, training, sampling, context, retrieval and tool use. Original numerical examples and a fictional cafe assistant show how the pieces fit together. Five recall questions with answers and a practical paper exercise. No prior technical knowledge required.

item.title: [Fitness] How Muscles Grow: Training, Recovery and Progress
item.description: Muscle growth explained through two fictional training logs: effort, rest, weekly volume, exercise selection, progression, food, recovery and plateaus. Includes five recall questions with answers and a low-risk exercise for reviewing a training log. General education for healthy adults, not an individual training prescription.

item.title: [Communication] How to Negotiate Without Giving Everything Away
item.description: Prepare alternatives, understand interests, trade across scope and timing, handle pressure, and reach clear agreements. A fictional design project develops into complete worked conversations, with five recall prompts and one practical exercise.

item.title: [Business & Money] Why Profitable Businesses Run Out of Cash
item.description: September 15 catch-up lesson: profit versus cash, contribution and break-even, pricing and discounts, financial statements, inventory, growth funding, and practical cash forecasting. Original worked business cases, five recall questions and one forecast exercise.

item.title: [Psychology] Why You Repeat Habits You Want to Break (Expanded)
item.description: Expanded edition: a full lesson on automatic habits, reinforcement, triggers, friction, practical plans and recovery. Worked cases cover distraction, reading, creative work and business administration. Replaces the original short edition.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] The First Test: How to Know What Helps.
item.description: A foundation for The Forge: evaluate claims, distinguish observation from explanation, and practise with a worked example. Revised edition with clearer dialogue, recall questions and a reading companion approach.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] The Filter
item.description: You own two hundred and forty books and believe almost none of it. That's the correct response, and here's what to do with it.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] Pilot 3: The Filter
item.description: Third pass. Dense, fluent, nothing wasted.

item.title: [Evaluating Books & Beliefs] The Nine
item.description: Segment one, the three piles. Segment two, six books off your own shelf under pressure, including Neville taken seriously. Segment three, the nine, and tonight's ten minutes of work.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] Pilot: The Filter
item.description: Cold open. Two hundred and forty books and the one thing that has to be installed before any of them count.
